catalog_entry.target: A count, sum or extreme of goals or match events aggregated across many matches in a tournament, relative to a strike or condition.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Twenty-two settled 2026 World Cup series, each a different statistic of the same 104 matches (72 group, 32 knockout incl. third place): a tournament goal sum; named-team goal ladders over the group stage or the full run (3 to 8 matches); extremes across teams or groups with $1/N dead heats; per-round shootout counts and the longest shootout in rounds; the highest-scoring knockout match and the fastest goal; group-table patterns and group winners lost in the Round of 32; a cross-match race to concede first by ET timestamp; whether the champion ever trails; and player or rare-event aggregates (hat tricks, club goal pools, a player scoring in every knockout round, direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals). Outcomes come from team strengths against the actual draw and simulated bracket, the international goal environment, shootout kick dynamics, player shares of team goals, and contract scope flags.

inputs.why: Per-team scored/conceded rates against the drawn opponents and the simulated knockout path settle the named-team ladders, Goals Allowed and the most/fewest extremes.
Group plus 32-team bracket simulation supplies matches played per team, champion identity and knockout pairings used by most series.
International attack/defence strength is the base of every match rate and of champion and pairing probabilities.
Goals per match level times 104 matches sets the Total Goals strike (308+ needs about 2.96 per match).
Shared tournament effects widen the totals distribution beyond independent matches.
Match-level goal count distribution is the building block for sums and maxima of match totals.
Tail of single-match totals drives the knockout Highest Scoring Game strike.
Mismatch mix of fixtures moves group goal totals, blanks, hat tricks and high-scoring games.
Per-round shootout counts (exactly N / N+ in R32, R16, QF) and group winners lost in the R32 come from round-level bracket simulation.
Per-tie probability of level after 120 minutes feeds every shootout-count series.
Knockout goal-rate and draw-rate multiplier changes shootout counts and the KO highest-score maximum.
Round count of each shootout settles Longest Penalty Shootout and when goalkeepers kick.
Team shootout skill slightly shifts shootout length and goalkeeper-kicker exposure.
Opening-goal timing per match sets the Fastest Goal minimum and early concession hazards.
Kickoff ET timestamps plus per-minute concession hazards settle the four-team Concede First race.
P(champion never trails) needs champion identity times conditional trailing along its path.
Recovery after conceding feeds the champion-never-trails calculation.
Excess blank rates of the weakest attacks dominate Every Team to Score.
Joint W/D/L patterns inside a group settle Group Points (all four teams on 4 points).
Draw frequency in balanced group fixtures is required for the all-on-4-points pattern.
Player-level goal distributions settle Hat Trick count, Club Goals maximum and Goal in Every Game.
Per-match base rates for direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals settle the rare-event series.
Player npxG/90 and shot share drive hat-trick and every-round scorer probabilities.
Expected minutes of key forwards cap team and player goal ladders.
Star-forward absence moves named-team goal ladders and player-pool aggregates.
Designated free-kick and corner takers drive direct free-kick and olimpico rates.
Qualification state before matchday 3 drives rotation and attacking intent in named-team ladders.
Dead-rubber versus must-score leverage moves weak teams' blank probabilities in round three.
Longer added time raises goals per match for Total Goals and team ladders.
Penalty award rate adds goals and feeds goal-environment estimates.
VAR penalties and disallowed goals shift the per-match goal level.
Heat and Mexico City/Guadalajara altitude act on a subset of venues and raise or lower rates.
Per-series flags: group vs full tournament, ET in or out, shootouts out, own-goal attribution, third-place game in.
Exact wording per series fixes strike construction (N+, exactly N, $1/N dead heats) and scope.

interactions.hypothesis: A full-tournament team ladder is a random sum: goals per match times a random number of matches, so advancement depth and attack strength compound and the upper rungs are convex in strength.
A shared tournament effect shifts every match together, so Total Goals has fatter tails than an independent sum of 104 matches.
The longest shootout is a maximum over a random number of shootouts, so per-round shootout counts and sudden-death continuation must be simulated jointly.
Never-trailing is evaluated on the eventual champion only, so it mixes over champion identity and conditioning on winning lowers trailing rates.

contract.settlement_definition: All 22 live series have settled (status finalized) rules text. YES conditions: KXWCTOTALGOAL all teams' goals over the full tournament incl. ET, own goals counted, third-place game included, N+ strikes (sample 308+); KXWCTEAMGOALS one named team's goals in the GROUP STAGE (regulation+stoppage), N+; KXWCTEAMTOTALGOALS one named team's goals over the FULL tournament incl. ET, N+; own goals credited to the benefitting country; KXWCGOALSALLOWED named team concedes zero in the group stage, own goals charged to the erring team; KXWCGSGOALS named team allows the most group-stage goals and KXWCGROUPGOALS named group scores the fewest group-stage goals, both with Yes $1/N dead heats; KXWCEVERYTEAMGOAL every team scores at least once; KXWCGAMEGOALS highest knockout match total incl. ET, shootout goals excluded, own goals counted; KXWCFASTESTGOAL earliest goal by official FIFA match minute across all matches; KXWCKOPENALTIES exactly N shootouts in a named round (sample: Quarterfinals); KXWCLONGESTPEN longest shootout measured in rounds, all No if no shootout; KXWCGOALIEPEN any goalkeeper scores in a knockout shootout; KXWCGROUPWINELIM at least N group winners lose in the R32; KXWCGROUPPTS any group with every team on 4 points; KXWCCONCEDE1ST first of Mexico, Spain, Argentina, Ghana to concede by ET timestamp, shootouts excluded, $1/N if none concede; KXWCWINNERTRAIL champion never trails in any match; KXWCHATTRICK at least N hat tricks incl. ET, excl. shootouts; KXWCCLUBGOALS maximum over clubs of goals by players under contract, N+; KXWCGOALEVERYGAME a player scores in each of R32, R16, QF, SF and Final (third place excluded); KXWCFREEKICKGOAL, KXWCOLIMPICO, KXWCGOALIEGOAL any such goal (goalkeeper open-play goal incl. ET, no shootout or own goals). Source of truth: official FIFA match records (only the fastest-goal text names FIFA explicitly).

rules_evidence.quote: If all teams collectively record at least 308 goals during the full tournament (including regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Total Goals is an all-team full-tournament sum including extra time with an N+ strike.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals count toward the total goals scored during the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup.
rules_evidence.establishes: Own goals are included in the tournament total.

rules_evidence.quote: If Germany records at least 18 goals during the group stage (including regulation and stoppage time)
rules_evidence.establishes: Team Goals is a single named team's group-stage goal ladder; no extra time is possible or counted.

rules_evidence.quote: If France records at least 22 goals during the full tournament (including regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Tournament Goals is a single named team's full-tournament ladder including extra time, so matches played (3-8) matter.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals scored by opposing players that benefit France count toward France's total goals
rules_evidence.establishes: Own goals are credited to the benefitting team in team ladders.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals are attributed as conceded goals to the team that made the error
rules_evidence.establishes: Goals Allowed is a named-team group-stage clean-sheet condition with own goals charged to the erring team.

rules_evidence.quote: If Uzbekistan records the most goals allowed by any team in the group stage
rules_evidence.establishes: Group Stage Goals is an extreme across 48 teams of goals conceded, not a goal-sum ladder.

rules_evidence.quote: If Group L records the fewest goals scored by any group in the Group Stage
rules_evidence.establishes: A group-level minimum across 12 groups, with $1/N payouts on ties.

rules_evidence.quote: Own goals scored by opposing teams count as a goal for the benefitting country.
rules_evidence.establishes: Every Team to Score credits own goals to the beneficiary.

rules_evidence.quote: goals scored during a penalty shootout do not count towards the total goals scored in a match
rules_evidence.establishes: Highest Scoring Game (KO) excludes shootout kicks; the sampled event is the knockout stage including ET.

rules_evidence.quote: The goal time will be determined by the official match minute as reported by FIFA.
rules_evidence.establishes: Fastest Goal is a minimum over all matches by official FIFA minute, not seconds.

rules_evidence.quote: If exactly 4 matches are decided by a penalty shootout in the Quarterfinals
rules_evidence.establishes: Shootout counts are per round with exact-count strikes.

rules_evidence.quote: a "round" refers to when both teams have each taken one penalty kick
rules_evidence.establishes: Longest shootout is counted in rounds of paired kicks.

rules_evidence.quote: If no matches are decided by penalty shootout in the knockout stage of the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup, then all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: No shootout means every rung settles No.

rules_evidence.quote: If any goalkeeper scores a goal during a penalty shootout in any match in the knockout stage
rules_evidence.establishes: Goalkeeper shootout goal depends on goalkeepers taking kicks, usually only deep into sudden death.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 9 group winners are knocked out in the Round of 32
rules_evidence.establishes: A count over the 12 group winners' R32 ties.

rules_evidence.quote: In order for all teams in a group to finish on 4 points, each team must win once, lose once, and draw once.
rules_evidence.establishes: Group Points requires a cyclic W-D-L pattern in at least one group.

rules_evidence.quote: determined by the official Eastern Time (ET) timestamp of the goal, regardless of the match minute, matchday, or tournament stage
rules_evidence.establishes: Concede First is a cross-match race decided by clock time, so the kickoff calendar matters.

rules_evidence.quote: Penalty shootout goals do not count towards conceding.
rules_evidence.establishes: Shootout kicks cannot trigger the race.

rules_evidence.quote: the market will still resolve to Yes as long as they never trailed in a match at any point throughout the tournament
rules_evidence.establishes: Settles on the eventual champion never trailing; draws and level scores are allowed.

rules_evidence.quote: A hattrick occurs when an individual player scores at least 3 goals in a game (stoppage and extra time included).
rules_evidence.establishes: Hat tricks include ET goals and are counted over both stages.

rules_evidence.quote: Player goals are attributed to the club they are currently under contract with.
rules_evidence.establishes: Club Goals pools goals by club contract; the 'currently' timing is not dated.

rules_evidence.quote: 'every knockout stage match' refers to all rounds of the knockout stage (excluding the third-place match)
rules_evidence.establishes: A player must score in all five knockout rounds, so only finalists' players are eligible.

rules_evidence.quote: a free kick goal is when a goal is scored directly from a free kick by the player taking the free kick
rules_evidence.establishes: Only direct free-kick goals credited to the taker count.

rules_evidence.quote: an "olimpico" goal is considered a goal that is scored directly from a corner kick
rules_evidence.establishes: Olimpico is a direct corner goal.

rules_evidence.quote: own goals committed by a goalkeeper do not count as a goal scored by that goalkeeper
rules_evidence.establishes: Goalkeeper goal is open play incl. ET; shootouts and own goals are excluded.

variants_and_edge_cases: Period scope differs inside the archetype: group-stage series (Team Goals, Goals Allowed, Group Stage Goals, Group Points) cannot include ET; full-tournament and knockout series (Total Goals, Tournament Goals, Highest Scoring Game KO, Hat Trick, Goalie Goal) include ET; no series counts shootout kicks as goals except Goalie Penalty Goal, which is only shootout kicks.

Own-goal attribution flips by series: credited to the beneficiary for Team Goals, Tournament Goals and Every Team to Score, charged to the erring team for Goals Allowed and Concede First, and counted in match totals for Total Goals and Highest Scoring Game.

Dead heats pay Yes $1/N rounded down to the cent for Group Stage Goals (most allowed), Group Stage Goals by group (fewest) and Concede First when none of the four concede; other series have no tie rule because they are N+ or exact counts.

Highest Scoring Game: only the 26KO event (incl. ET) is in the sampled rules; the independent reviewer reports a separate 26GS group-stage event '(including regulation and stoppage time)', not present in the pack (see unresolved gs_highest_game_wording_unverified).

Longest Penalty Shootout is counted in rounds of paired kicks; a shootout ending after the first team's kick in a round (possible inside the first five) leaves the final round partial, and the text does not say whether it counts.

Club Goals attributes goals to the club 'currently under contract'; loanees, free agents and players moving during the tournament are not addressed. Goal in Every Game excludes the third-place match, so only the two finalists' players can be YES.
Winner to Trail does not say whether conceding first in a shootout or trailing on aggregate in a shootout counts; goals only are mentioned, so shootouts are presumably excluded.

KXWCCLUBGOALS secondary text contains a template sentence about 'Own goals scored by USA's players' that has no meaning for a club-pool maximum; own goals are presumably not credited to any club, but the text does not say so.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official FIFA match records (KXWCFASTESTGOAL names 'the official match minute as reported by FIFA'); the other sampled texts do not name a source, so FIFA match reports are assumed as source of truth.

mechanism.summary: All 22 series are statistics of the same 104 matches but read different parts of them. Sums: Total Goals adds every match incl. ET; named-team ladders add one team's matches over the group stage (three games, no ET) or the full run (three to eight games incl. ET), so attack strength against the actual drawn opponents and advancement depth dominate. Extremes: the most goals allowed by a team, the fewest goals by a group, the highest-scoring knockout match, the fastest goal, the longest shootout and the biggest club goal pool are maxima or minima whose probabilities depend on tails and on how many candidates compete. Counts: shootouts per knockout round, group winners lost in the R32, hat tricks and rare goal types. Patterns and paths: a cyclic 4-4-4-4 group table, a four-team race to concede by wall-clock time, and the champion never trailing. A shared tournament factor correlates matches, and per-series scope flags (ET, shootouts, own-goal direction, $1/N dead heats) change the random variable.

stages.name: Tournament goal level for the all-team total
stages.description: Total Goals sums 104 match totals including extra time and own goals. World Cup goals per match ran about 2.6 to 2.7 through 2022 and the 48-team field adds weaker teams, while the long-added-time directive adds minutes. The 308+ sampled rung needs about 2.96 per match, so the level, its shared tournament shock and directive effects decide the series rather than any one team.
stages.distribution: Sum of overdispersed match counts plus a tournament random effect; approximately normal in the middle with fatter tails than an independent sum.

stages.name: Named-team and per-group goal sums and their extremes
stages.description: Team Goals (group stage) and Tournament Goals (full run incl. ET) are one country's goals against its three drawn opponents plus any knockout opponents; Goals Allowed asks for a group-stage clean sheet with own goals charged to the erring team; Group Stage Goals takes the team conceding the most and the group scoring the fewest, both paying $1/N on ties; Every Team to Score is a conjunction effectively decided by the weakest attacks' three group games. Star availability and matchday-3 rotation move the sums.
stages.distribution: Per-team sums are compound Poisson-gamma counts over a random number of matches (3-8); extremes across 48 teams or 12 groups are discrete order statistics with frequent ties.

stages.name: Knockout rounds: shootout counts, upsets and shootout length
stages.description: Matches to go to Penalties counts ties level after 120 minutes within a named round (16, 8 or 4 ties), at roughly a quarter of World Cup knockout ties historically and higher for balanced pairings; Group Winners Eliminated counts group winners losing R32 ties against runners-up or third-placed teams; Longest Penalty Shootout is the maximum round count across all shootouts; Goalie Penalty Goal needs a goalkeeper to kick, usually only after ten outfield kickers in sudden death.
stages.distribution: Per-round counts are sums of dependent Bernoullis with pairing-specific probabilities; shootout length is five rounds or fewer with about 27% reaching sudden death and then a geometric tail with ratio near 0.58.

stages.name: Single-match extremes: highest knockout score and fastest goal
stages.description: Highest Scoring Game (sampled 26KO event) is the maximum total over 32 knockout matches including extra time, shootout kicks excluded and own goals counted, so it depends on mismatched KO pairings, cagey knockout play and ET goals added to level ties. Fastest Goal is the minimum over 104 matches of the first-goal official minute; with roughly 100 matches an 8th-minute-or-earlier goal is likely, so the opening-period hazard drives it.
stages.distribution: Maximum of discrete match totals (extreme of a Poisson mixture) and minimum of censored first-goal times; both are steep functions of the per-match tail.

stages.name: Cross-match race and champion path properties
stages.description: Concede First is the earliest ET timestamp at which Mexico, Spain, Argentina or Ghana concede, so the kickoff calendar (Mexico played the opening match) and each team's concession hazard against its specific opponents decide it, with $1/N if none concede. Winner to Trail follows the eventual champion across seven or eight matches: probability is a mixture over champion identity of never being behind, and conditioning on winning reduces trailing.
stages.distribution: Race outcome is a categorical over four teams dominated by schedule order; never-trailing is a path Bernoulli whose mixture is concentrated on a few favourites.

stages.name: Group-table patterns
stages.description: Group Points pays if any of the twelve groups ends with every team on four points, which needs each team to win one, draw one and lose one. This is a joint pattern of six results that is most likely in balanced groups with high draw rates, and matchday-3 situations where a draw suits both sides add mass; it cannot be read from teams' marginal points.
stages.distribution: Rare joint event per group (low single-digit percent at most for balanced groups); union over twelve nearly independent groups.

stages.name: Player and rare goal-type aggregates
stages.description: Hat Trick counts players with three or more goals in a match (ET included), concentrated in mismatch group games; Club Goals takes the maximum over clubs of goals by players under contract, driven by clubs with many forwards at deep-running nations; Goal in Every Game needs a finalist's player to score in R32, R16, QF, SF and Final. Free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals are rare goal types with type-specific base rates and taker effects.
stages.distribution: Player goals are thinned team counts; hat-trick and rare-event counts are near-Poisson with small means; the club maximum is an order statistic over correlated pools.

stages.name: Per-series scope and payout rules
stages.description: The verified texts change the random variable per series: group-stage series exclude ET by construction, full-tournament and knockout series include it, shootout kicks never count as goals except in Goalie Penalty Goal, own goals go to the beneficiary in team ladders but to the erring team in Goals Allowed and Concede First, three series pay $1/N on ties and Longest Shootout settles all No without a shootout.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the text; reading a flag wrongly shifts team ladders by a goal or flips extreme-market payouts.

soc.tournament_goal_environment.label: Tournament goals-per-match environment from past World Cups and tournament-specific drivers
soc.tournament_goal_environment.mechanism: Expected goals per match across a whole tournament, set by the mix of strong and weak teams, the group format and rule directives such as added time and VAR.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.rationale: Total goals is a sum of 104 correlated matches, so the level matters more than any one team. Past World Cups sit around 2.6 to 2.7 goals per match but a 48-team field adds more lopsided group games, and a longer-added-time directive raises totals. A model built from club league averages misses the tournament-specific level.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.measurement: For each World Cup since 1998: goals per match incl. ET split by group stage and knockout, by rating-gap bucket and by added-time directive era (2022 onward longer). Fit a Poisson-gamma mixture across matches; set the 2026 mean from team ratings of the actual 48-team field through the draw, shrunk to the historical mean with k=3 tournaments. Output expected and distribution of the 104-match sum incl. ET and own goals. As-of = after the draw; update after each round.
free_sources: FIFA match reports and historical results datasets (free)
raw_data: match-level goals by stage and tournament
soc.tournament_goal_environment.why: Settles KXWCTOTALGOAL (all teams, full tournament incl. ET, own goals counted): the strike is goals per match times 104; it is only context for single-team ladders.

soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.label: Shared tournament-wide factor affecting all matches' scoring
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.mechanism: Common causes that move every match together: ball, climate, officiating directives, travel burden and a low-scoring or high-scoring tournament style.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.rationale: Match outcomes within a tournament are not independent: one referee directive on penalties or a heat wave across venues shifts the whole distribution. Ignoring this makes the variance of totals and counts too narrow, which matters most for tail strikes such as a record goals total.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.measurement: Estimate the between-tournament variance of per-match goals residual after team strength, using World Cups and continental finals since 2000 (random effect per tournament); report the intraclass correlation and its posterior. Use the implied standard deviation as the dispersion widening for tournament sums. As-of = pre-tournament; update only with documented directive changes.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.why: Governs how wide the distribution of tournament totals and event counts is beyond independent-match noise.

soc.shootout_length_distribution.label: Penalty shootout length and per-kick conversion distribution
soc.shootout_length_distribution.mechanism: A shootout lasts five rounds each unless decided early, then sudden death; its length is a stopping-time of kick conversions.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.rationale: The longest shootout is an extreme of a small random number of shootouts. With kick conversion p near 0.70 at World Cups, a shootout is level after five rounds with probability about 0.27 and each sudden-death round continues with probability p^2+(1-p)^2 (about 0.58), so P(9+ rounds) per shootout is roughly 0.05. Goalkeepers usually kick only from round 11, so Goalie Penalty Goal depends on the same tail.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.measurement: From all World Cup shootouts since 1982 (34 through 2022) plus Euro, Copa America, AFCON and Asian Cup shootouts (well over 100 in total), compute per-kick conversion with beta shrinkage (prior mean 0.70, strength 40 kicks), the probability of a level score after five rounds, the sudden-death continuation probability, and P(length>=k rounds) under the paired-kick definition, including the share of shootouts ending mid-round. Combine with soc.ko_round_outcome_counts to give the distribution of the maximum. As-of = bracket known.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.why: Directly specifies KXWCLONGESTPEN (rounds, all No without a shootout) and the exposure of goalkeepers kicking for KXWCGOALIEPEN.

soc.group_gap_composition.label: Distribution of strength gaps across scheduled group and knockout matches
soc.group_gap_composition.mechanism: The tournament's schedule fixes a list of pairings whose strength gaps determine how many lopsided and how many balanced matches occur.
soc.group_gap_composition.rationale: Goal totals and trailing events depend on gap: lopsided matches produce more goals and fewer comebacks, balanced ones more draws and shootouts. A 48-team field has more lopsided group games than 32 teams, so past World Cup rates cannot be applied unadjusted.
soc.group_gap_composition.measurement: Using pre-tournament team ratings and the final draw, compute for each of the 72 group matches the rating gap and the implied goal expectations; bucket into quintiles and compare with past World Cups' bucket frequencies. As-of = after the draw.
soc.group_gap_composition.why: Moves group-stage goals and every-team-scores events by changing the mix of mismatch fixtures.

soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.label: Per-team goals scored and conceded expectations over the team's actual fixtures and simulated path
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.mechanism: A named team's tournament goals are the sum over its three drawn group opponents and any knockout opponents of match-level scoring rates, with the number of matches random from 3 to 8.
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.rationale: Team Goals and Tournament Goals are single-team ladders, not tournament totals; Goals Allowed, most-allowed and fewest-by-group extremes need the conceding side. A strong attack drawn with two weak sides can post 8+ group goals, and full-tournament totals depend on advancement depth. Rotation in matchday 3 after qualification is secured and star-forward absence lower the sum; own goals are credited to the beneficiary for scoring and to the erring team for conceding.
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.measurement: For each team and each scheduled or simulated fixture: lambda_for and lambda_against from a Dixon-Coles international model (attack/defence, half-life 2 years, friendlies weighted 0.5, shrink k=10 matches to confederation mean) adjusted for venue altitude/heat and for knockout via soc.knockout_cagey_factor; ET adds 30 minutes at 0.8x rate in level KO ties. Sum over the comp_sim path (20000 draws) to output the distribution of group-stage goals, full-tournament goals and group-stage goals conceded per team, plus group sums. Matchday-3 rotation multiplier from soc.group_stage_scenarios. As-of = draw, updated after each match.
raw_data: international match results with goals and venue
soc.team_tournament_goal_expectation.why: Primary for KXWCTEAMGOALS, KXWCTEAMTOTALGOALS, KXWCGOALSALLOWED, KXWCGSGOALS, KXWCGROUPGOALS and KXWCEVERYTEAMGOAL.

soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.label: Per-round knockout outcome counts from bracket simulation (shootouts per round, group winners lost in R32)
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.mechanism: Each knockout round has 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1 ties whose pairings come from the bracket; the count of ties level after 120 minutes and the count of group winners losing in the R32 are sums of dependent Bernoullis over that round's simulated pairings.
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.rationale: Historical World Cup knockout shootout frequency is about a quarter of ties (2014 4/16, 2018 4/16, 2022 5/16), far above a few percent, and balanced pairings raise it. Contracts are per round ('exactly 4' in the Quarterfinals), so the needed object is the per-round count distribution, not a tournament binomial. Group winners face third-placed or runner-up teams in the R32, so upset counts depend on the 495-combination allocation.
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.measurement: In each comp_sim draw, record for each round the number of ties level after 120 minutes, using P(level after 90) from the joint goal model times P(level after ET | level at 90) calibrated to soc.method_path_tree_calibration-style counts for World Cups and continental finals since 1986 (beta shrinkage k=30 ties per node), and the number of group winners eliminated in the R32. Output P(count = n) per round for n=0..ties. As-of = after each completed round.
soc.ko_round_outcome_counts.why: Settles KXWCKOPENALTIES per round and KXWCGROUPWINELIM, and gives the number of shootouts for KXWCLONGESTPEN and KXWCGOALIEPEN.

soc.concession_race_schedule.label: Cross-match concession race: kickoff ET timestamps and per-minute concession hazard of named teams
soc.concession_race_schedule.mechanism: The first of several named teams to concede is the minimum over their matches of the clock time of their first goal conceded; earlier kickoffs give a head start that opponent-specific hazards then modify.
soc.concession_race_schedule.rationale: Concede First is settled by ET timestamp regardless of match minute or matchday, so a team playing first in the calendar (Mexico played the 11 June opening match) has a large structural edge; a strong defence playing days later rarely beats an early kickoff. If none of the four concede in the tournament, Yes pays $1/N, which matters only for strong defences with long clean-sheet runs.
soc.concession_race_schedule.measurement: Per match, conceding intensity h(t)=lambda_against*f(t) with f estimated as the historical share of goals per minute bucket (0-15, 15-30, 30-45+, 45-60, 60-75, 75-90+) from World Cup/Euro goal minutes since 1998 normalised to mean 1 per 90; first half 45+U(1,5) min, half-time 15 min, second half 45+U(2,8) min. Convert match minute to ET wall-clock using official kickoff time; simulate 100000 times the first concession timestamp across all named teams' matches (earliest wins); P(no concession in all matches) separately. As-of schedule fixed; update after each match.
free_sources: FIFA match schedule with kickoff times (free)
Historical minute-by-minute goal times (Wikipedia/FIFA reports, free_scrape)
soc.concession_race_schedule.why: Primary for KXWCCONCEDE1ST, which soc.first_goal_hazard (within-match identity) cannot settle alone.

soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.label: Probability the eventual champion never trails, mixed over champion identity and path
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.mechanism: P(YES) = sum over teams of P(team wins the tournament and never trails in any of its 7-8 matches); trailing requires conceding while level or ahead turning to behind, and winning a match conditions on mostly leading.
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.rationale: The contract follows the champion, not any match winner. Conditioning on winning seven or eight matches sharply lowers the trailing rate, and strong favourites with elite defences dominate the mixture. Recent champions mostly trailed at least once (e.g. Argentina 2022 lost its opener to Saudi Arabia), so the base rate is low but highly path dependent.
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.measurement: In each tournament simulation draw simulate each match's goal times (inhomogeneous Poisson from match lambdas with the soc.score_state comeback multipliers) through 120 minutes; the champion 'trails' if at any moment in any of its matches it is behind in goals; penalty-shootout kicks do not count. P = fraction of draws in which the eventual champion never trails; report decomposition by champion. Validate vs. never-trailed share of 1986-2022 World Cup champions (shrink to simulation with k=5 tournaments). As-of pre-tournament, rerun after each match with realised states.
free_sources: Historical goal minutes of champions (Wikipedia/FIFA reports, free_scrape)
raw_data: goal minutes for past champions' matches
soc.champion_path_trailing_probability.why: Primary for KXWCWINNERTRAIL; replaces the within-match first_goal_hazard x response interaction that ignored champion identity.

soc.group_table_pattern_probability.label: Joint W/D/L pattern probability within each group (cyclic 4-4-4-4 tables)
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.mechanism: All four teams on 4 points requires each team to have exactly one win, one draw and one loss; this is a specific joint pattern of six results with two draws and four decisive matches arranged cyclically.
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.rationale: The probability is small per group and highest in balanced groups with high draw rates; it is not a function of any team's marginal points. Twelve groups make the any-group event materially more likely than one group, and matchday-3 incentives (a draw suiting both sides) can raise the draw count.
soc.group_table_pattern_probability.measurement: From the comp_sim group simulation (20000 draws) record each group's final points vector and the indicator that all four equal 4; use Dixon-Coles match probabilities with soc.draw_propensity adjustment for balanced pairs and a matchday-3 mutual-draw uplift estimated from World Cup and Euro group stages since 1998 (shrunk to zero with k=30 matches). Output P(any of 12 groups). As-of = draw, updated after each matchday.

soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.label: Player-level tournament goal distributions with club attribution and knockout-round continuity
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.mechanism: Each player's tournament goals are his share of team goals per match times minutes, summed over the team's matches; club pools sum players by club contract, hat tricks are per-match counts of 3+, and every-round scoring needs a goal in each of five knockout matches.
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.rationale: Hat Trick counts concentrate in mismatch group games and in teams with a dominant finisher; Club Goals maximum is driven by clubs with many attackers at deep-running nations (Real Madrid, Manchester City, Bayern, PSG types); Goal in Every Game needs a finalist's player to score in five straight knockout matches, a tiny probability concentrated on penalty-taking strikers of favourites.
soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.measurement: Per player in the 26-man squads: npxG/90 and penalty duty (soc.player_xg, soc.penalty_taker_status logic) shrunk toward a position prior (k=900 minutes), expected minutes per match from soc.player_minutes_expectation, share of team lambda = player xG share. Per simulated match draw player goals as Poisson-thinned team goals (incl. ET). Output distribution of tournament hat tricks, max club total (club from squad list at tournament start), and P(any player scores in R32..Final). As-of = squad lists, updated with injuries and lineups.

soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.label: Per-match base rates of direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.mechanism: Each of these goal types is a rare event per match; P(at least one in 104 matches) = 1 - exp(-104 * rate) adjusted for taker quality, with rates differing by many orders of magnitude.
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.rationale: Direct free-kick goals occur a few times per World Cup (so YES is likely), olimpicos are rare (well under one per tournament on average) and open-play goalkeeper goals are almost unheard of at World Cups outside late set pieces; a model must use type-specific base rates rather than goal totals. Elite free-kick takers present raise the first.
soc.rare_goal_event_base_rates.measurement: From event data for World Cups, Euros and Copa Americas since 2010: counts of goals by type (direct free kick credited to taker, direct corner, goalkeeper scorer excluding own goals and shootouts) per match; Poisson rate with gamma prior from top-5 league rates per match (prior strength 200 matches); adjust free-kick rate by the share of squads with a designated taker whose club direct-FK conversion is above league median. As-of = squad lists.

soc.goal_dist.reason: Match goal distribution (international, incl. ET where the series counts it) is the unit summed for Total Goals and maximised for Highest Scoring Game.

soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.reason: The sampled Highest Scoring Game event is the max over 32 knockout matches incl. ET; tail dispersion of KO totals by gap bucket sets the 4+ style strikes.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: Per-tie probability of being level after 120 minutes, calibrated to the ~25% World Cup KO shootout rate, feeds per-round shootout counts.

soc.penalty_shootout_skill.reason: Team skill differences barely move shootout length or goalkeeper-kick exposure relative to kick noise; context only.

soc.first_goal_hazard.reason: Opening-goal timing per match is the core of Fastest Goal (minimum over 104 matches); for Concede First it is a component of the ET-timestamp race.

soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.reason: Comeback hazards enter the champion-never-trails simulation but only conditional on champion identity; club-fitted values need national-team calibration.

soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.reason: Every Team to Score is effectively a group-stage conjunction: the binding weak attacks play only three matches, so their excess blank rates dominate.

soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.reason: Scope flags now verified per series: group vs full tournament, ET in/out, shootouts out, own-goal attribution direction and third-place inclusion differ across the 22 series.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules text is available for all 22 series and fixes strike construction (N+, exactly N, $1/N dead heats) and scope; versioned text must be stored per event.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Group and bracket simulation gives matches played per team, KO pairings per round and champion identity, which several series cannot be priced without.

soc.ratings.reason: International attack/defence ratings set every match rate; they must be fitted on years of internationals, not club data.

soc.knockout_cagey_factor.reason: Lower KO goal rates and higher draw rates directly change shootout counts and the knockout highest-score maximum.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: Group Points needs two draws in a cyclic pattern; draw propensity of balanced pairs is the key component.

soc.player_xg.reason: Player npxG share drives hat-trick, club-pool and every-round-scorer probabilities via soc.tournament_player_scoring_pool.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes of key forwards cap named-team ladders and player aggregates; matchday-3 rotation is the main swing.

soc.injuries.reason: A star forward missing group games moves a named team's group-goal ladder by a goal or more; minor for tournament-wide totals.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Presence of elite direct free-kick and in-swinging corner takers shifts the free-kick and olimpico rare-event rates.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Qualification state before matchday 3 determines rotation and must-score intent for named-team ladders and every-team-scores.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Dead-rubber index refines matchday-3 blank and draw rates; overlaps with group_stage_scenarios so context only.

soc.added_time.reason: The long-added-time directive since 2022 adds minutes and goals per match, shifting Total Goals and team ladders.

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Penalty frequency is embedded in goal-environment estimates; tracked only to adjust for a tournament directive.

soc.var_intervention_rate.reason: VAR-awarded penalties and disallowed goals change the goal level slightly; context for the environment input.

soc.weather.reason: Summer heat at several US venues and altitude at Mexico City/Guadalajara modify rates for a subset of matches; context to the environment level.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of a very high-scoring match rises convexly with the strength gap, so a knockout bracket that keeps a few heavy mismatches in the R32 lifts the KO Highest Scoring Game rungs more than the same average gap spread evenly.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the KO maximum from real simulated pairings versus pairings with equal mean gap but compressed spread.

interactions.mechanism: A tournament-level random effect makes Total Goals a mixture, so the 104-match sum has fatter upper and lower tails than independent matches; rungs far from the mean such as 308+ are most affected.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tournament random-effect variance across World Cups and continental finals and compare 308+ probability with and without it.

interactions.mechanism: The longest shootout exists only if at least one tie reaches penalties and long ones need sudden death; with about four or five shootouts per tournament the maximum and the chance a goalkeeper kicks are driven jointly by count and length.
interactions.how_to_test: Joint simulation of shootout counts per round and lengths versus a model using a fixed average count.

interactions.mechanism: A full-tournament team ladder equals goals per match times matches played; stronger teams score more per match and play more matches, so high rungs (e.g. 22+ for France) respond multiplicatively to strength while group-stage ladders do not.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare full-tournament team-goal distributions from the joint simulation with a fixed-match-count approximation for favourites versus minnows.

interactions.mechanism: Champions that trail must come back, so conditioning on the title selects paths with few or recovered deficits; the never-trailed probability is far above the product of unconditional per-match trailing rates for a favourite.
interactions.how_to_test: On World Cups 1986-2022 compare champions' never-trailed frequency with the unconditional per-match never-trailed rate of the same teams.

interactions.mechanism: In the Concede First race, a team whose first match ends before another team kicks off wins outright if it concedes at all, so the race is a threshold on kickoff order: earlier calendar position dominates defensive strength unless the early team keeps a clean sheet.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with real kickoff timestamps versus all four teams kicking off simultaneously and compare the race probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: A weak team still without a goal entering matchday 3 with qualification hope chases harder; one already eliminated may not, so the Every Team to Score conjunction is sensitive to round-three incentives of the few binding teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare blank rates in matchday-3 World Cup group matches by stakes bucket against matchdays 1-2.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear mean effect on the sum but convex effect on far tail rungs
nonlinearities.why: Total Goals moves linearly with the per-match level, but the probability of clearing a high rung such as 308+ changes much faster than the mean because it sits in the tail of a mixture.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at five or fewer rounds, then geometric decay with ratio p^2+(1-p)^2
nonlinearities.why: With kick conversion p about 0.70 each sudden-death round continues with probability about 0.58, so P(9+ rounds) per shootout is near 0.05 and the longest-shootout ladder falls steeply.

nonlinearities.shape: Product over 48 teams dominated by the weakest few
nonlinearities.why: Every Team to Score is a product of per-team scoring probabilities over three group matches, so one or two weak attacks with excess zero rates set most of the probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Minimum over 104 matches: fastest-goal rungs saturate near certainty for late minutes
nonlinearities.why: With about 100 matches, even a modest per-match chance of a goal by minute 8 makes the 8th-minute rung likely and earlier rungs drop sharply, so the response is concave in the hazard.

catalog_entry.label: Tournament matchup composition and host venue
catalog_entry.target: Whether a named pair of teams is confirmed as the matchup in any match, a named round or a final (settled at qualification), or whether any tournament game is played in a named host country/state.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Pair-matchup contracts settle the moment both named teams qualify for the same match: in any World Cup match (group co-membership is fixed by the draw, otherwise the pair must converge in a knockout slot), in a named World Cup round (Semifinal, USA Quarterfinal with a 'No Team' outcome), or in the Champions League final after the league phase, two-leg knockout rounds and a fixed bracket. Probabilities come from the joint group, best-third and knockout simulation pushed through the official slot graph. The location series is different: it settles on whether a scheduled game is actually played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July 2026, a host-venue relocation and cancellation risk unrelated to results.

inputs.why: Joint probability the two named teams occupy the same match (any round, a named round or the final) is the settled quantity for four of the five series with rules text (and, provisionally, KXWCFINALMATCHUP).
Maps group positions and best-third combinations to knockout slots and rounds, the structure every World Cup pairing uses.
Joint cross-group finishing distribution including the best-third ranking feeds slot occupancy.
Group and knockout simulation produces the joint paths from which pair meetings are counted.
International and club strength ratings set each match probability that fills the bracket.
Group tie-breaks and best-third criteria decide slots near the cut.
Single-leg World Cup ties and two-leg Champions League ties, incl. ET and shootouts, decide who advances.
Champions League league-phase rank distribution determines which clubs enter the knockout bracket and where.
UEFA rank-to-bracket-line mapping fixes which side of the Champions League bracket each finisher is on, so whether two clubs can only meet in the final.
Aggregate state between legs updates Champions League advancement during the knockout rounds.
Opponent strength along a team's World Cup path sets its reach probability per round.
Remaining group permutations during the group stage move slot probabilities.
Long-term absences of key players adjust team strength for advancement.
Risk that scheduled host-city games are moved or cancelled settles the location series.
Abandonment or postponement of the specific scheduled games in a host region can leave a location unplayed.
Exact wording fixes any-match vs named-round vs final, settlement at qualification, the No Team outcome and the location granularity.

interactions.hypothesis: Whether two teams from different groups can meet in a given round depends on the best-third combination that qualifies, so pair-meeting probability needs the joint cross-group distribution pushed through the slot graph.
Two Champions League clubs on the same bracket side can only meet before the final, so P(final pairing) is near zero for same-side finishes and multiplicative across rounds for opposite sides.
A host location settles No only if every scheduled game there is moved or not played, so the location probability is a near-certain base state with a small joint failure regime.

contract.settlement_definition: Six live series: five with settled rules text and KXWCFINALMATCHUP, which has no listed market (NO_LISTING) and only Kalshi series metadata (title 'World Cup Final Matchup', scope 'Future', terms WCTEAMSINGAME.pdf, sources ESPN and FIFA; metadata, not rules text, fetched 2026-11-09; the terms PDF was unreadable), so it is assumed, not verified, to settle like the sibling pair series on which two teams meet in the final. KXWCTEAMSINGAME: YES if the named pair 'is confirmed to be the matchup in any match' of the 2026 World Cup (any round incl. group stage and, by the any-match wording, the third-place game), resolving 'immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played'. KXWCMATCHUP: same, restricted to 'the Semifinal' (ticker suffix SEMI2 suggests a specific semifinal slot). KXWCUSAOPPONENT: USA vs a named team in any Quarterfinal; if USA does not reach the Quarterfinals the 'No Team' outcome resolves Yes. KXTEAMSINUCL: the named pair are the two finalists of the 2026 Champions League Final; forfeit or disqualification after qualifying still resolves Yes and reaching a series stage counts. KXWCLOCATION: YES if 'a 2026 FIFA World Cup game is played in Mexico before Jul 20, 2026' (country or US state granularity), independent of which teams play. None of the sampled texts names a settlement source; FIFA/UEFA official announcements are assumed.

rules_evidence.quote: If USA vs England is confirmed to be the matchup in any match in the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: Teams in Game asks whether the pair meets in any match, so the quantity is the sum over rounds of meeting probabilities, not one numbered match.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution occurs immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement happens at qualification; the match need not be played.

rules_evidence.quote: If Norway vs Switzerland is confirmed to be the matchup in the Semifinal of the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup
rules_evidence.establishes: World Cup Matchup restricts the pairing to the Semifinal round.

rules_evidence.quote: If USA does not advance to the Quarterfinals, then the market titled "No Team" resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: USA Opponent is a mutually exclusive structured market over QF opponents plus a No Team outcome.

rules_evidence.quote: If the team qualifies but later forfeits, is disqualified, or cannot participate for any reason after qualifying, the market still resolves to Yes as qualification was achieved.
rules_evidence.establishes: Champions League Final Matchup settles on qualification; later withdrawal does not reverse it.

rules_evidence.quote: For series-based games, advancing to that series stage satisfies the criterion.
rules_evidence.establishes: Two-leg ties count by advancement to the stage.

rules_evidence.quote: If a 2026 FIFA World Cup game is played in Mexico before Jul 20, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Location settles on a game actually being played in a host country/state by a deadline, not on bracket composition.

variants_and_edge_cases: Scope varies across series: any match (Teams in Game), a named round (Semifinal; USA in a Quarterfinal) and a single final (Champions League); a pair from the same World Cup group meets with certainty in the group stage under the any-match wording.

Settlement is at qualification for all pairing series, so a later forfeit, injury crisis or postponement does not change the outcome; the location series instead requires the game to be played before 20 July 2026.
KXWCUSAOPPONENT is structured: exactly one of the named opponents or 'No Team' resolves Yes, so probabilities must sum to one across outcomes.
KXWCMATCHUP ticker 26SEMI2 suggests the second semifinal slot specifically while the text says 'the Semifinal'; a pair meeting in the other semifinal may settle differently.
The KXTEAMSINUCL secondary text is truncated after 'Mathematical possib', so the treatment of mathematically clinched qualification before the deciding match is not visible.
KXWCLOCATION does not define 'played' for a match that kicks off and is abandoned, nor whether a relocated match within the same country still counts.

KXWCFINALMATCHUP has no listed market and no rules text; Kalshi metadata (scope 'Future', terms WCTEAMSINGAME, the same terms id as KXWCMATCHUP) suggests the pair-in-a-match template, but whether it means the final only, the champion pair or any-match is not read.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled texts. Assumed FIFA and UEFA official bracket/fixture announcements for pairings and FIFA match records for location; the independent reviewer reports that Kalshi lists FIFA, ESPN, Fox Sports and the New York Times for location, which the pack does not show (unresolved location_settlement_source).

series_mapping_issues.issue: Settles on whether any World Cup game is played in a named host country/state before a deadline; the outcome does not depend on bracket progression or team identity, only on host-venue operations, relocation and cancellation risk.

mechanism.summary: Four of the five series with rules text ask whether a named pair of teams is confirmed in the same match, and they settle the moment both qualify. For the World Cup the probability is the sum over rounds of joint slot occupancy: same-group pairs meet with certainty under the any-match wording, other pairs need group finishes and best-third combinations that route them to a common R32 to Final slot and then wins in every feeding single-leg tie. Named-round variants (Semifinal; USA in a Quarterfinal with a No Team outcome) restrict the sum to one round. The Champions League final pairing follows a different structure: league-phase rank, two-leg playoff and knockout ties, and a fixed bracket that only lets opposite-side clubs meet in the final. The location series is unrelated to results: it settles on whether any scheduled game is actually played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July, a host-operations risk. KXWCFINALMATCHUP (no rules text) is priced provisionally as a named pair meeting in the final.

stages.name: World Cup slot graph and settlement scope
stages.description: The regulations fix which group positions feed which R32 slot, the annex lookup for the eight best third-placed teams across 495 combinations, and the tree from R32 to the final and third-place match. Each pairing contract reads this graph with its own scope: any match, the Semifinal only, or USA's Quarterfinal, all settled at qualification rather than at kickoff.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; the only uncertainty is transcription error or an amendment, which would change which pairs can meet in a round.

stages.name: World Cup group finishing and best-third cut
stages.description: Twelve groups of four play three rounds; finishing order follows the tie-break sequence and the eight best of twelve third-placed teams qualify. Which groups supply those eight decides their R32 slots, so a team's possible opponents depend on results in other groups. Strength ratings must come from years of international results, and matchday-3 permutations matter while groups are live.
stages.distribution: Joint discrete distribution over 12 group orderings plus a cross-group third-place ranking with frequent ties on points resolved by goal difference.

stages.name: World Cup knockout convergence of a named pair
stages.description: Two teams in different groups meet only if both win every tie feeding a common slot; settlement happens once the second team qualifies for that match. P(meet) sums over the rounds where their potential paths cross; for the Semifinal variant only one round counts, and for USA Opponent the outcome is a categorical over QF opponents plus No Team. Path difficulty and ET/shootout resolution of single-leg ties enter. KXWCFINALMATCHUP (NO_LISTING, metadata only) is priced provisionally as the final-slot case of the same convergence; its settlement wording is unknown.
stages.distribution: Sum over rounds of joint products of dependent Bernoulli advancements; strongly correlated because the two paths share potential opponents.

stages.name: Champions League final pairing
stages.description: The 2026 Champions League final pairing comes from the 36-club league phase (ranks 1-8 straight to the R16, 9-24 into a two-leg playoff), then two-leg R16, quarterfinal and semifinal ties on a seeded bracket fixed by rank. Two clubs on the same bracket side cannot both reach the final, so the pairing probability is the product of each side's path probabilities given ranks, updated with aggregate state between legs.
stages.distribution: Mixture over league-phase ranks of products of two-leg advancement probabilities; zero mass for same-side combinations.

stages.name: Host-region game actually played
stages.description: Game Location settles on whether any 2026 World Cup game is played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July. Each region has several scheduled matches, so NO requires a region-wide failure: political or security relocation from a host city, a stadium becoming unavailable, or every scheduled match being abandoned. Team identity and bracket results are irrelevant; dated news about relocation is the only moving signal.
stages.distribution: Near-certain YES base state with a small, news-driven regime-switch probability of region-wide relocation.

talent_strength.note: National-team and club strengths fill both brackets.

opponent_matchup.note: Which opponents a pair must beat to converge; UEFA bracket sides.

role_personnel.note: No player-named series remain after KXWCPLAY was refiled to unreg:player_appearance_selection; squad composition enters only through team ratings and the injuries context input.

availability_news.note: Long-term key absences for advancement; dated relocation news for the location series.

environment.note: Host-region operations decide the location series.

game_context_script.note: ET, shootouts and two-leg aggregate states decide who advances.

pace_volume.note: Outcomes are pair occupancy of a slot or a venue being used, not counts of events, so no opportunity-volume input applies to any of the six series.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and shootout conversion affect advancement only through match and tie probabilities already produced by ratings and the advancement tree; no contract counts a per-opportunity rate.

settlement_contract.note: Any-match vs round vs final scope, settlement at qualification, No Team outcome, location deadline.

soc.bracket_slot_graph.label: Official tournament match graph: slots, match numbers, venues and third-place allocation
soc.bracket_slot_graph.mechanism: The published schedule fixes which slot plays which, in what stadium and on what date; entrants to each knockout slot come from group finishing positions through a fixed mapping.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.rationale: Whether two teams can meet, and in which round, is fixed by structure: group winners and runners-up feed defined R32 slots, the eight best third-placed teams are assigned by an annex lookup depending on which groups they come from, and later slots follow the tree to the final and third-place match. A single wrong cell changes which pairs can meet in a Semifinal or a Quarterfinal, so the graph must be read from the regulations.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.measurement: Transcribe the regulation's match list into a directed graph: nodes are match numbers with date, city and stadium; edges map group position (1st, 2nd, best 3rd by combination) to slot. Encode the third-place table as a function of the set of qualifying third-place groups and validate that every combination yields a legal bracket. Test by checking against the official bracket for a hypothetical result. As-of = regulations publication; re-fetch if amended.
free_sources: FIFA competition regulations and match schedule (free)
raw_data: match schedule with numbers, dates, venues
soc.bracket_slot_graph.why: Maps group positions and best-third combinations to knockout slots and rounds so pair-meeting probabilities can be summed per round; venue/date fields are needed only for schedule checks.

soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of group finishing positions across all groups
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.mechanism: Simulated finishing order in each group plus the cross-group ranking of the twelve third-placed teams, from which the eight best advance.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.rationale: Which team lands in a knockout slot depends on not just its own group but on the other groups through the best-thirds ranking. The cross-group coupling makes marginal group probabilities insufficient: the combination of third-place qualifiers decides slot assignment and so venue.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.measurement: Simulate all group games with the team goal model, apply the group tie-break order transcribed from the 2026 regulations (secondary reports: points, then head-to-head points, goal difference and goals among tied teams, then overall goal difference and goals, then conduct score and FIFA ranking; unverified until Article 13 is read), rank third-placed teams on points, goal difference, goals scored, conduct and ranking, and output the joint distribution of slot occupants for each knockout match. 20000 draws minimum. As-of = last completed match.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.why: Feeds soc.pair_meeting_probability and P(USA in a given Quarterfinal slot) through the slot graph.

soc.pair_meeting_probability.label: Probability a named pair of teams is confirmed as the matchup in any match, a named round or a final
soc.pair_meeting_probability.mechanism: For two teams, P(meet) = 1 if drawn in the same group (any-match wording), otherwise the sum over knockout rounds r of P(both occupy the two slots of the same round-r match), computed from the joint simulation because their paths share opponents.
soc.pair_meeting_probability.rationale: Teams in Game, Matchup, USA Opponent and the Champions League final all settle on joint slot occupancy at qualification. Marginal reach probabilities multiplied together are wrong: two teams on the same bracket side can meet only once and only before the final, and the best-third allocation makes cross-group meetings depend on other groups. Settlement at qualification means the R32-onward meeting is fixed as soon as both win the feeding ties.
soc.pair_meeting_probability.measurement: In each comp_sim draw (World Cup) or UEFA knockout simulation draw (Champions League), record for every pair the round in which they are confirmed in the same match (group, R32, R16, QF, SF, third place, final) and for USA the QF opponent or none. Output P(meet in any match), P(meet in round r) and the categorical over USA QF opponents including No Team; Monte Carlo standard error below 0.002 for pairs above 1%. As-of = after each completed match.
soc.pair_meeting_probability.why: Settled quantity for KXWCTEAMSINGAME, KXWCMATCHUP, KXWCUSAOPPONENT and KXTEAMSINUCL.

soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.label: Risk that scheduled World Cup games in a named host country/state are moved or not played
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.mechanism: A host region settles YES if at least one of its scheduled games is played there before the deadline; NO requires every scheduled game in the region to be relocated, cancelled or abandoned before being played.
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.rationale: Mexico had 13 scheduled matches (Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey) and Massachusetts (Foxborough) several, so NO needs a region-wide failure: security events, political action to move games from certain US cities, immigration/visa disputes or stadium unavailability. The base rate is very low but the risk is news-driven and clustered, and it is independent of team results.
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.measurement: For region r with n_r scheduled matches: base per-match relocation/cancellation hazard h0 = (relocated or cancelled matches)/(scheduled matches) in World Cups, Euros, Copa Americas and Olympics since 1990, Beta(0.5,50)-shrunk; region-level decision probability q_r from a dated news-flag ladder (0 none, 1 official statement of discussion, 2 formal FIFA review) with q_r = 0.002/0.03/0.20 priors, updated by Bayes with timestamped reports. P(no game in r) = q_r + (1-q_r)*h0^(n_r) assuming within-region independence given no decision. As-of = latest news timestamp.
raw_data: scheduled matches per host region with dates
soc.host_venue_relocation_risk.why: Primary for KXWCLOCATION; bracket inputs are irrelevant to it.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Group and knockout simulation is the engine for World Cup pairings; it must output per-round joint slot occupancy so pair meetings and USA QF opponents can be counted.

soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.reason: With KXTEAMSINUCL now filed here, the UEFA rank-to-bracket mapping is the structural input that decides whether two clubs can meet only in the final; it is not used for World Cup series.

soc.bracket_path_difficulty.reason: Opponent quality along a team's path sets per-round reach probabilities, a component of pair meetings; subsumed by the full simulation when it runs.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Group tie-break order and best-third criteria decide slots near the cut and therefore which pairs can meet in a round; order is unverified against the regulations.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: During the group stage it enumerates remaining outcomes and slot destinations; irrelevant once groups finish.

soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.reason: Single-leg World Cup ties and two-leg Champions League ties (with KXTEAMSINUCL in scope) both need the regulation/ET/shootout tree.

soc.injuries.reason: Only a long-term absence of a key player shifts team strength enough to matter for advancement; no player-named series remains in this archetype.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: For KXWCLOCATION, abandonment or postponement of the scheduled games in a region is one of the two routes to NO; irrelevant to pairing series, which settle at qualification.

soc.ratings.reason: International ratings (World Cup) and club ratings (Champions League) set the match probabilities; must be fitted on multi-year histories, not current-tournament results.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules text distinguishes any-match, named-round and final scopes, settlement at qualification, the No Team outcome and location granularity.

soc.uefa_league_phase_simulation.reason: Champions League league-phase ranks determine direct R16 entry, playoff pairings and bracket position for KXTEAMSINUCL.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Two-leg Champions League ties update between legs; used only for KXTEAMSINUCL during the knockout rounds.

interactions.mechanism: Whether two teams from different groups can meet in the R32 or R16 depends on which other groups supply qualifying third-placed teams, so pair-meeting probabilities from independent group marginals pushed through the graph misstate cross-group pairings.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare pair-meeting probabilities from the joint simulation with those from independent group marginals mapped through the annex.

interactions.mechanism: Teams level on points flip group position at a hard tie-break threshold (head-to-head before overall goal difference per secondary reports), moving a team onto a different bracket side and changing which pairings are possible.
interactions.how_to_test: Re-simulate with head-to-head and overall goal difference swapped and count pairs whose meeting probability changes by more than 1 point.

interactions.mechanism: A late-round meeting requires both teams to win every feeding tie, so per-round advancement probabilities multiply along two paths; modest per-round edges compound into large differences in Semifinal pairing odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated Semifinal pairing probabilities with the product of single-team reach probabilities for same-side and opposite-side pairs.

interactions.mechanism: In the Champions League, two clubs whose league-phase ranks put them on the same bracket side can meet before the final but never in it, so the final-pairing probability is zero for those rank combinations and positive only for opposite sides.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate simulated final pairings by league-phase rank combination and confirm zero mass for same-side combinations.

interactions.mechanism: With several scheduled games per region, individual abandonments almost never empty a region; NO needs a region-level relocation regime, so the location probability is a mixture of a near-certain base state and a rare switch driven by dated news.
interactions.how_to_test: Review relocations in major tournaments since 1990 and compare per-match abandonment rates with region-level relocation events.

nonlinearities.shape: Step change at the best-eight third-place cut
nonlinearities.why: Only eight of twelve third-placed teams advance, so a small goal-difference change moves a team from exit to a specific R32 slot and switches which pairs it can meet.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero, one or a product depending on bracket geometry
nonlinearities.why: Same-group pairs meet with certainty under any-match wording, same-side pairs can meet only before the final, and opposite-side pairs only late; the probability is discontinuous in bracket position rather than smooth in strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Near-zero baseline with a jump on credible relocation news
nonlinearities.why: Region-wide relocation is a discrete official decision, so the NO probability stays near zero until dated announcements move it in steps.
